text: Have you experienced any manic episodes in the past, such as periods of unusually high energy or decreased need for sleep? I also need to know if there is any family history of mood disorders or psychosis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the seven-month duration of auditory hallucinations preceding the depressive symptoms, I need to rule out primary psychotic disorders. Have you noticed any disorganized speech or behavior, or a significant decline in your ability to perform daily activities independent of your mood?

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the hallucinations began before the mood symptoms and you lack disorganized behavior, I need to clarify if the voices are present when you are not feeling sad. Do the voices persist even during moments when your mood is relatively stable, or do they only appear when you are depressed?

speaker: Patient
text: The voices are constant and don't seem to depend on my mood; they were mocking me even before I started feeling this persistently sad. They are always there, regardless of how I feel emotionally.

speaker: Doctor
text: The persistence of hallucinations independent of mood strongly suggests a primary psychotic disorder rather than a mood disorder with psychotic features. To differentiate between schizophrenia and schizoaffective disorder, I need to know if you have experienced any periods of at least two weeks where you had clear mood symptoms (depression or mania) but no psychotic symptoms.

speaker: Patient
text: No, I haven't had any periods where the voices stopped while I was still feeling sad. The hallucinations have been continuous for seven months, overlapping with the four months of depression.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the psychotic symptoms have persisted throughout the entire duration of the mood episode, this points toward Schizophrenia rather than Schizoaffective Disorder. speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of negative symptoms like social withdrawal and flat affect, combined with continuous hallucinations and a major depressive episode, strongly supports a diagnosis of Schizoaffective Disorder, Depressive Type. DIAGNOSIS READY: Schizoaffective Disorder, Depressive Type
